annotationRationale: The solution identifies altitudes using perpendicularity and finds their intersection. The two-point slope formula and point-slope equation provide the needed altitude equation.
sourceMethod: Follows the official intersection of the altitudes through A and C, starting with horizontal BC. Omits the optional third-altitude confirmation.

review.mathCheck: Horizontal BC gives altitude x=2. Since AB has slope −2/3, the altitude through C has equation y=3x/2. Their intersection is (2,3), also lying on the third altitude y=4x−5. The coordinate sum is 5, choice A; the exterior intersection is valid.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 11, pages 8–9, with the two altitudes introduced in reverse order. The result agrees with the official figure. The official third-altitude confirmation is optional because concurrency is given.
review.annotationCheck: The horizontal/vertical case and finite negative-reciprocal slope case are handled separately. The altitude, perpendicularity, and intersection nodes are appropriately assessed; slope computation and point-slope form supply background tools.
